notes: Test/retest on the measurement itself: Priya re-derived order-to-handoff time for 10 already-collected orders from the POS ticket log plus the pickup tally sheet, twice, two days apart, blind to her first pass (first-pass sheet stayed in the drawer). Items are real order_ids from wait-times.csv, picked to span the observed range (6.0 to 11.1 min); first readings match the recorded dataset values. Gauge increment is the recording resolution, 0.1 min. USL 5.0 is the customer walk-away line (VoC S4); no LSL -- a fast drink has no lower limit, so the engine names its denominator as study variation, not tolerance. Resolution pre-check: 0.1-min increments on the ~5-minute observed span. Single-operator repeatability only -- the caveat the engine prints is part of the record.
gauge_name: POS ticket log + pickup-counter tally sheet (same POS clock), read to 0.1 min
